Use the model above to compute the following result. Express your answer as a fraction in its lowest terms.

$\frac{3}{4}÷\frac{6}{7}=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
The denominators are $4$ and $7.$ We can make a common denominator of $4\times 7=28.$ 

We split the shape on the left of the division sign into $7$ parts vertically, and we split the shape on the right into $4$ parts horizontally:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14155061/assets/919b2e3f87aabf375cb968e876ee19b0ce9cd6a70c41088b062459a1f4f1f133.png)

So, our division problem now is

$$
\frac{21}{28}÷\frac{24}{28}.
$$

Since the denominators are equal, this is equivalent to

$$
21÷24=\frac{21}{24}=\frac{7}{8}.
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\frac{3}{4}÷\frac{6}{7}=\frac{7}{8}.
$$
